paper_id: Learning Fine-Grained Grounded Citations for Attributed Large Language Models__oa_W4402670531
title: Learning Fine-Grained Grounded Citations for Attributed Large Language Models
motivation: LLMs hallucinate and current attributed systems suffer from suboptimal citation quality due to reliance on in-context learning, with citations too coarse for users to pinpoint specific evidence
problem_framing: Teach LLMs to generate responses where each statement cites specific extractive quotes (not just document IDs), requiring high-quality attributed training data and proper grounding-guidance architecture
key_insight: First extract supporting quotes from source documents (grounding), then condition the generation process on those quotes — this provides supervision signals AND serves as fine-grained attribution
method_signature: Two-stage training: Grounding Guided Generation (extract quotes → guide generation) + Consistency-Aware Alignment via DPO to align grounding with attribution
evaluation_criteria: Citation quality (precision/recall/F1 via TRUE) and correctness (EM/claim recall) on ASQA/ELI5/QAMPARI
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: FRONT encounters lower Rec.-5 on QAMPARI dataset because answers consist of concatenated entities, diverging significantly from training data
evidence_for_taste: citations are typically presented in the form of either document identifiers
complicate the process for users to pinpoint exact supporting evidence
such discrepancies challenge the attempt to employ these grounding quotes
the nature of its answers, which consist of concatenated entities, diverging significantly from our training data
thinking_moves: 把引用粒度从文档级降低到句子级 quotes
先做 grounding 再 guided generation 的两阶段 pipeline
用弱模型 (7B) 监督强模型偏好训练的 weak-to-strong 思路
对 citation quality 和 correctness 分别评估, 承认两者 trade-off
